cells.tense: The receiving is working, and it stays joined to what gets done with it.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you noticed that you would normally keep, and leave it with them as said, not as advice.
cells.core:
The receiving is working, and it has not cost you the room. Things arrive before they are spoken — the shift in a voice, the subject nobody is touching — and that arrival stays joined to what gets done next. That join is why people feel steady around you.

Two currents are in play: all the feeling still possible with someone, and what is already known about them. Mostly they run together. When they do not, you catch it, and catching it is most of the work. Put one hunch into speech this week — half-formed, no case built underneath. Say it once and watch what comes back. That keeps the receiving in use instead of stored up.
cells.sheetLine: You pick things up early and keep them moving.

cells.tense: You are already in the next conversation, feeling out what it might ask of you.
cells.ask: Pick one person you have been reading hard and go a week without predicting them — let whatever they say next be news.
cells.core:
You are a step ahead of the room, and the step is costing the room. People get read fast — what they will want, what will land badly, how it goes — and lately the reading is so fast that the conversation arrives already decided. There is a bracing for a version of it no one has handed over yet.

The same skill, held back from running ahead, lets you choose from what is actually here. Whatever has been rehearsed for them — one exchange where you are half-ready, say the thing, then wait and see what it does. That is the receiving half, still in the room while you act. One exchange, then stop. Being ready is not the requirement for being present.

cells.tense: The door that closed is still standing between you and the person in front of you.
cells.ask: Do one thing for one person today without being asked and without explaining it afterward.
cells.core:
Seeing people clearly is available and it is not being used. A shift in a face gets caught, and then it gets set down, because acting on it moves things closer to people, and closer is a place you are not currently standing. So it stays at a distance: observe, know, touch nothing.

Putting something back out into the world is how it gets collected again. One small thing for one person — no asking first, no explaining after. Let the response stand as it comes. What has gone quiet is the doing-with-what-is-seen, and that comes back by use rather than by waiting.
cells.sheetLine: You still see it. You just stopped acting on it.

cells.tense: Reading the room is already happening and it gets filed as nothing in particular.
cells.ask: Name one read made this week that shaped what got done, out loud, to someone who was there: 'You went quiet and I changed what I said.'
cells.core:
People are already being read — the pause before an answer, the detail that does not fit, what someone needs before they say it. It runs constantly, so far back that it gets described the way a schedule gets described, as just how things go. A read happens, then whatever got done because of it gets called something else.

One plan got moved around a thing somebody could not say, and that got called logistics. Something was softened at the edges because of how it would land. Saying one such read out loud is not boasting — it puts an address on it, so what gets picked up is given as well as taken. Said once to the person it was about, that is enough.
cells.sheetLine: You have been reading people and calling it nothing.

attempts.check: The record does not say anyone said no — Too Little locates a closed door behind the person, but the cause, the person behind it, and how long ago it stands are mine, so I keep it to the unreached handle and the unasked question. The reader could say the caution is not damage but good judgment, so the ask must not require trusting again. The ask survives by spreading one part of one thing across one shelf, which costs nothing and holds whether the reading is right or wrong. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any closing line about the handle being passed and kept safe alongside the reading — cut it.
